message.content:
### The “Best” Sushi Spots in Los Angeles (as of 2026)

> *“Best” is always a matter of taste, but the following places consistently earn top marks from critics, food‑bloggers, and locals alike. They cover a range of styles—from traditional Edomae to modern fusion—and span the city’s major neighborhoods.*

| # | Restaurant | Neighborhood | Style & Highlights | Price Range | Why It Stands Out |
|---|------------|--------------|--------------------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | **Sushi Gen** | Little Tokyo | Classic Edomae, hand‑rolled nigiri, seasonal Omakase | $200–$300 (Omakase) | 30‑year legacy, Michelin‑starred, renowned for its meticulous fish selection. |
| 2 | **Sushi Park** | West Hollywood | Contemporary omakase, creative rolls, high‑end sake list | $250–$350 (Omakase) | Awarded “Best Omakase” by LA Weekly; chef’s tasting menu changes weekly. |
| 3 | **Nobu Los Angeles** | Beverly Hills | Fusion of Japanese & Peruvian, signature black cod | $80–$120 (per plate) | Celebrity hotspot, Michelin‑starred, offers a chic dining experience. |
| 4 | **Kazuya** | West Hollywood | Traditional Edomae, minimalist décor, focus on sashimi | $70–$120 (per plate) | Known for its “Sashimi of the Day” and a quiet, intimate setting. |
| 5 | **Sushi Tatsu** | Downtown LA | Classic sushi, affordable, great for casual nights | $30–$60 (per plate) | Popular among locals for its value and consistent quality. |
| 6 | **Sushi Kappo** | Santa Monica | Kappo style, seasonal tasting menu, ocean view | $150–$250 (Omakase) | Combines a seaside vibe with a refined menu; great for special occasions. |
| 7 | **Sushi Saito** | West Hollywood | Ultra‑exclusive, limited seating, 3‑course tasting | $300–$400 (Omakase) | One of the few LA spots with a 3‑star Michelin rating; reservation required months in advance. |
| 8 | **Matsuri** | Koreatown | Fusion of Japanese & Korean flavors, creative rolls | $50–$90 (per plate) | Unique blend of cultures, vibrant atmosphere, and a popular happy hour. |

#### How to Choose

| Preference | Recommended Spot |
|------------|------------------|
| **Traditional Edomae** | Sushi Gen, Kazuya |
| **Modern Fusion** | Nobu, Matsuri |
| **Value & Casual** | Sushi Tatsu |
| **Luxury Omakase** | Sushi Park, Sushi Kappo, Sushi Saito |
| **Scenic View** | Sushi Kappo (Santa Monica) |

#### Quick Tips

1. **Reservations** – For Omakase or Michelin‑starred spots, book 2–3 months ahead.  
2. **Dress Code** – Many upscale sushi bars enforce a smart‑casual dress code.  
3. **Sake Pairing** – Ask for a sake flight; many places offer curated selections that complement the menu.  
4. **Dietary Needs** – Most restaurants can accommodate gluten‑free or low‑sodium requests; just let the host know.

---

**Want a personalized recommendation?** Let me know your budget, preferred neighborhood, or any dietary restrictions, and I’ll narrow it down further!
